title: Segmented residency lanes, thaw-on-demand, and wavefront prefill scheduling for paged attention
creator: Luis Ortega
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency and memory churn for long-context paged-attention workloads by introducing segmented residency lanes, a thaw-on-demand eviction model, and wavefront prefill scheduling that coordinates kernel selection with prefill decoding.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile end-to-end decode latency reduced by >=10% on 16k-context long-chat workload compared to baseline runtime-1.20 with current paged KV policies
GPU VRAM peak decreased by >=6% for mixed short+long sessions under production traffic profile (simulated workload)
No regression on median latency for short 1–2k context requests (<=2% change)
All new config knobs behind feature flag with telemetry and enrichment events emitted to the console dashboard
notes: This ticket explores an alternative to global LRU eviction: split the KV pool into short-residency and long-residency lanes. Pages are promoted/demoted based on a decay score computed from clocked access patterns and prefill predictions. We also implement a 'thaw-on-demand' flow where evicted cold pages can be brought back lazily during prefill with prioritized micro-batching to avoid single-request stalls. Kernel selection will be guided by predicted prefill width: narrow prefill windows choose low-overhead kernels while wide wavefront prefill uses optimized attention kernels and fused-kernel paths.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Luis Ortega: Kickoff meeting notes attached to design doc. We agreed on three experimental knobs: lane sizes, decay half-life, and thaw budget per-prefill.
2026-02-23 - Maya Chen: Initial allocator prototype done. Segmented lanes implemented as soft partitions with dynamic rebalancing based on occupancy; benchmark harness ready.

2026-03-01 - Omar Patel (review): Asked for microbench for cold reinflation path — we need a 95th tail breakdown for 'thaw-on-demand' vs 'eager-fetch'. Added PR comment to include synthetic workload where 30% of sessions are cold-start long-context.

2026-03-05 - Maya Chen: Microbench results: thaw-on-demand shows 12% 95th reduction on synthetic long-context workload vs eager-fetch, but adds a 1.8% median regression on short queries. Plan: implement per-route soft quotas to protect short-query SLAs.

2026-03-08 - Design feedback from Priya Rao: prefer 'hysteresis with decay curves' instead of fixed thresholds to avoid thrash on bursty workloads. Updated design & impl to use exponential decay with tunable half-life.

2026-03-10 - QA: Added stress test where thousands of small sessions interleave with occasional 32k fills. Observed compaction stalls under single-threaded sweep; filed follow-up ENG-87001 for cooperative compaction sweeps.
2026-03-12 - Maya Chen: Rolling out feature flag to canary region; telemetry shows occupancy heatmap and per-prefill thaw counts emitting as expected. Next: tune thaw budget to meet short-query SLA.
